openings.claim: A certificate-driven paired review could support a reproducible further-evaluation decision despite selective label unavailability.
openings.delta: Refine G0085:R1: separate acquisition ranking from decision certification. In a spreadsheet or local script, maintain possible candidate-minus-baseline correctness gains for each flagged row, then total and slice intervals. Inspect threshold-relevant rows in the slice currently at the loss boundary first, then total-gain-relevant rows; use record identifiers for ties. Recompute after each returned label and remove unavailable rows from acquisition candidates while retaining their uncertainty.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, balanced slice-quota inspection with identifier ordering, boundary-first review may obtain a supported decision with fewer adjudications. Distinguishing observations are certified decisions, remaining interval widths, labels consumed and elapsed time. Equal efficiency, more unresolved outcomes, or disagreement with the full-label key defeats the proposed advantage. Accessible pivotal rows and affordable interval computation are necessary; neither is established.
openings.probe: Run both policies on the supplied matched copies with independently reset sixteen-label allowances and seventy-minute limits; withhold the four preselected rows. Log every selection, returned label, unavailable attempt and time. Advance only when total lower gain is at least four and every slice lower gain is at least minus two. Reject only when total upper gain is below four or some slice upper gain is below minus two. Otherwise report unresolved, including inconclusive interval combinations. Freeze decisions, affected-slice summaries and logs before opening the full-label key. Compare support and resource use; this probes review policy, not deployment readiness.
assumptions: Supplied records identify flagged rows and provide a label vocabulary sufficient to bound possible gains; missing information forces unresolved.
Bounds include every permissible label completion; coarse bounds may remain inconclusive.
Unavailable attempts consume no adjudication allowance; time and logging still matter.

assessment: Preserves the acceptance rule and uncertainty reporting. Boundary-first acquisition is an unmeasured hypothesis; a cap alone cannot establish informative feasibility.

lineage.reason: Retains bounded paired review and comparative probe; specifies boundary-first acquisition and conservative interval certificates.
